features.name: Indus
features.fact: Originates in the Kailash region of Tibet; flows through Ladakh and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Its major tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
features.hook: Kailash region → Ladakh → Pakistan → Arabian Sea
features.recallPrompt: Rises in the Kailash region, crosses Ladakh and drains Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Jhelum
features.fact: Rises at the Verinag spring in Kashmir; flows through Srinagar and Wular Lake before continuing towards Pakistan.
features.recallPrompt: Rises at Verinag, flows through Srinagar and passes through Wular Lake.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Chenab
features.fact: Formed by the Chandra and Bhaga at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh; continues through Jammu and Kashmir into Pakistan.
features.recallPrompt: Formed at Tandi by the Chandra and Bhaga streams.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Ravi
features.fact: Rises in the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh and belongs to the Indus river system.
features.recallPrompt: Rises in Himachal Pradesh’s Chamba district; one of the five Punjab rivers.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Sutlej
features.fact: A major Indus tributary originating near the Manasarovar region in Tibet; enters Himachal Pradesh near Shipki La and feeds Gobind Sagar at Bhakra.
features.hook: Tibet → Shipki La → Gobind Sagar → Punjab
features.recallPrompt: Enters India near Shipki La and feeds the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Ganga
features.fact: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag; their combined flow is called Ganga. Major tributaries include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Son.
features.recallPrompt: Its two main Himalayan headstreams meet at Devprayag.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Godavari
features.fact: Rises at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and flows to the Bay of Bengal; major tributaries include Manjra, Indravati, Wardha and Wainganga.
features.recallPrompt: Rises at Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district and drains eastwards to the Bay of Bengal.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Krishna
features.fact: Rises near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra and flows to the Bay of Bengal; Bhima and Tungabhadra are major tributaries.
features.hook: Mahabaleshwar → Bhima / Tungabhadra → Bay of Bengal
features.recallPrompt: Rises near Mahabaleshwar; receives Bhima and Tungabhadra.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Narmada
features.fact: Rises at Amarkantak and flows westwards into the Gulf of Khambhat; Tawa is a major tributary.
features.hook: Amarkantak → westward valley → Gulf of Khambhat
features.recallPrompt: Rises at Amarkantak and flows west to the Gulf of Khambhat.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Tapi / Tapti
features.fact: Rises near Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh; flows through Maharashtra and Gujarat to the Arabian Sea near Surat.
features.recallPrompt: Rises near Multai in Betul district and flows west via Maharashtra and Gujarat.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Kaveri / Cauvery
features.fact: Rises at Talakaveri in Karnataka’s Brahmagiri hills; its basin spans Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry.
features.hook: Talakaveri → Karnataka → Tamil Nadu → Bay of Bengal
features.recallPrompt: Rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.

features.name: Brahmaputra / Yarlung Tsangpo
features.fact: Flows through Tibet as the Tsangpo, enters Arunachal Pradesh as Siang/Dihang and flows through Assam into Bangladesh.
features.recallPrompt: Known as Tsangpo in Tibet and Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh.
features.coordinateNote: Simplified study line; use the river centreline layer for the mapped course.
